Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>

2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

763:113.3c Triggered abilities have a trigger condition and an effect. They are written as “[Trigger condition], [effect],” and include (and usually begin with) the word “when,” “whenever,” or “at.” Whenever the trigger event occurs, the ability is put on the stack the next time a player would receive priority and stays there until it’s countered, it resolves, or it otherwise leaves the stack. 1124:Example: A player who controls Boon Reflection, an enchantment that says “If you would gain life, you gain twice that much life instead,” attacks with a 3/3 creature with wither and lifelink. It’s blocked by a 2/2 creature, and the defending player casts a spell that prevents the next 2 damage that would be dealt to the blocking creature. The damage event starts out as [3 damage is dealt to the 2/2 creature, 2 damage is dealt to the 3/3 creature]. The prevention effect is applied, so the damage event becomes [1 damage is dealt to the 2/2 creature, 2 damage is dealt to the 3/3 creature]. That’s processed into its results, so the damage event is now [one -1/-1 counter is put on the 2/2 creature, the active player gains 1 life, 2 damage is marked on the 3/3 creature]. Boon Reflection’s effect is applied, so the damage event becomes [one -1/-1 counter is put on the 2/2 creature, the active player gains 2 life, 2 damage is marked on the 3/3 creature]. Then the damage event occurs.

518:107.7. Each activated ability of a planeswalker has a loyalty symbol in its cost. Positive loyalty symbols point upward and feature a plus sign followed by a number. Negative loyalty symbols point downward and feature a minus sign followed by a number or an X. Neutral loyalty symbols don’t point in either direction and feature a 0. [+N] means “Put N loyalty counters on this permanent,” [-N] means “Remove N loyalty counters from this permanent,” and [0] means “Put zero loyalty counters on this permanent.” Loyalty symbols may also appear in abilities that modify loyalty costs.
1103:120.3c Damage dealt to a planeswalker causes that many loyalty counters to be removed from that planeswalker.
1188:122.1e The number of loyalty counters on a planeswalker on the battlefield indicates how much loyalty it has. A planeswalker with 0 loyalty is put into its owner’s graveyard as a state-based action. See rule 704.
1535:209.1. Each planeswalker card has a loyalty number printed in its lower right corner. This indicates its loyalty while it’s not on the battlefield, and it also indicates that the planeswalker enters the battlefield with that many loyalty counters on it (see rule 306.5b).
1729:306.5b A planeswalker has the intrinsic ability “This permanent enters with a number of loyalty counters on it equal to its printed loyalty number.” This ability creates a replacement effect (see rule 614.1c).
1731:306.5c The loyalty of a planeswalker on the battlefield is equal to the number of loyalty counters on it.
1739:306.8. Damage dealt to a planeswalker results in that many loyalty counters being removed from it.
2721:606.4. The cost to activate a loyalty ability of a permanent is to put on or remove from that permanent a certain number of loyalty counters, as shown by the loyalty symbol in the ability’s cost. This cost may be modified by other effects.
2723:606.5 If the total cost to activate a loyalty ability contains multiple costs to add or remove loyalty counters, those costs are combined into a single cost to add or remove loyalty counters, as appropriate.
2724:Example: A player controls Carth the Lion, which says, in part, “Planeswalkers’ loyalty abilities you control cost an additional [+1] to activate. That player also controls a planeswalker with three loyalty counters. To activate one of that planeswalker’s abilities that normally costs [+1], they put two loyalty counters on it. To activate one of its abilities that normally costs [−4], they remove three loyalty counters from it.
2726:606.6. A loyalty ability with a negative loyalty cost, taking into account any additional costs, can’t be activated unless the permanent has at least that many loyalty counters on it.
4102:Example: A player controls a planeswalker with three loyalty counters that is being attacked by a 1/1 with no abilities and a 7/7 with trample over planeswalkers. The active player could assign 1 damage from the first attacker and 2 damage from the second to the planeswalker and 5 damage to the defending player from the creature with trample over planeswalkers.
5116:702.150a Compleated is a static ability found on some planeswalker cards. Compleated means “If this permanent would enter with one or more loyalty counters on it and the player who cast it chose to pay life for any part of its cost represented by Phyrexian mana symbols, it instead enters the battlefield with that many loyalty counters minus two for each of those mana symbols.”
7488:A keyword ability that causes a planeswalker to enter the battlefield with fewer loyalty counters if a player chose to pay life for Phyrexian mana symbols in its cost. See rule 702.150, “Compleated.”

Activate Kiora’s +1 loyalty ability, untapping all three mana sources and the Weaver.  

Now you have seven mana sources available.  

Cast Memory with {4}{U}{U} (tapping all seven sources).  

Memory returns the two Metalwork Coloss 10/10s to the battlefield (as 2/2s after the Splendid counters already placed on them).  

Activate Kiora’s −2 loyalty ability to draw the top four cards of your library and put the two Forests into your hand.  

You now have seven mana sources again.  

Cast Mockery of Nature with {9} (tapping all seven sources), destroying one Metalwork Colossus.  

Cast Commit with {3}{U} (tapping the remaining four sources), returning the second Metalwork Colossus to the graveyard.  

Activate Kiora’s −8 loyalty ability, creating three 8/8 Octopus tokens and giving you the emblem.  

The three Octopi fight the two remaining 2/2 Metalwork Colossus (one Octopus kills each).  

You win this turn.

The only way to produce sufficient attackers/damage while reliably removing both blockers (regardless of how the opponent might block) is to unlock Kiora’s ultimate. This requires an extra loyalty counter, which Quarry Hauler supplies.

1. Cast Quarry Hauler ({3}{G}) targeting Kiora. Its ETB ability puts a second loyalty counter on Kiora (loyalty now 8).
2. Activate Kiora’s –8. You receive the emblem “Whenever a creature you control enters, you may have it fight target creature” and create three 8/8 Octopus tokens.  
   The three simultaneous ETB triggers are stacked so they resolve in the following order (targets chosen on placement):  
   - Octopus A fights Colossus X. Both deal 8 damage; A dies and X is left with 8 damage marked (effectively 2 toughness).  
   - Octopus B fights the same Colossus X. Both deal damage; X dies and B is left with 2 damage marked.  
   - Octopus C fights Festering Mummy. Both deal damage; Mummy dies and C is left with 1 damage marked.  
3. Festering Mummy’s dies trigger resolves; put a –1/–1 counter on any remaining creature you control that is not Hapatra or Weaver of Currents (e.g., Quarry Hauler or an Octopus).  
   Hapatra’s ability triggers and creates a 1/1 Snake token with deathtouch.  
4. The Snake’s ETB trigger (from the emblem) resolves; the Snake fights the remaining Colossus Y. The Snake’s deathtouch damage destroys Y.  
5. Both Metalwork Colossi are gone. Proceed to combat and attack with Hapatra and Weaver of Currents. They are unblocked and deal exactly 4 damage.

(The remaining cards in hand are not required.)

<solution>
1. Cast Quarry Hauler targeting Kiora (put a loyalty counter on her, now 8).
2. Activate Kiora’s –8 (emblem + three 8/8 Octopus tokens).
3. Order the three fight triggers: Octopus A vs. Colossus X, Octopus B vs. same Colossus X, Octopus C vs. Festering Mummy.
4. After Mummy dies, put its –1/–1 counter on any creature other than Hapatra/Weaver; Hapatra creates a deathtouch Snake.
5. Snake fights (and kills) the last Colossus.
6. Attack with Hapatra and Weaver for 4.
</solution>
